dedupe_keys.name: multi model hydropower projections for the us federal power marketing areas under cmip5 climate change

description: This data set gives ensembles of monthly hydropower generation projections for US federal hydropower plants, for 1966 to 2005 and 2011 to 2050, to show how climate change may affect federal hydropower. It was published in 2022 by Tian Zhou, Shih-Chieh Kao, Wenwei Xu, Sudershan Gangrade and Nathalie Voisin, as part of the federal assessment of climate effects on hydropower. Ten global climate models under RCP8.5 were downscaled with the RegCM4 regional model and run through the VIC hydrology model; runoff was turned into generation by two models, the WRES statistical approach and the process-based WMP approach using MOSART-WM river routing and reservoir operations, calibrated to monthly generation from the federal utilities. The study covers 132 plants built or run by the US Army Corps of Engineers, the Bureau of Reclamation and the International Boundary and Water Commission, aggregated to the Bonneville, Southeastern, Southwestern and Western Area Power Administrations and their subregions. Coverage is the United States federal hydropower fleet. Files are two MATLAB files, one per model, with a readme, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: only one emissions scenario is used, and results are aggregated, not per plant. Simulation uses are drought and climate adaptation planning for hydropower supply. Related records: data-wecc-ads-2034-hydropower covers western hydropower operations.
